clauses.reason: Sec. 1 commands that all executive departments, independent establishments and other governmental agencies, including their field services, "shall be closed on" April 27, 1994, as a mark of respect for Richard Milhous Nixon, and treats that day as within the scope of 5 U.S.C. 6103(b) and of all statutes relating to the compensation and leave of employees. It covers one day and ends by its own terms on April 27, 1994, recorded inclusive; the exclusive reading (the closing ends when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see.

Sec. 2 provides that the first sentence of section 1 does not apply to offices and installations, or parts of them, that the agency heads determine should remain open for reasons of national security or defense or other public reasons. It limits the closing of April 27, 1994 and operates only on that day, so it ends with the closing on 1994-04-27, recorded inclusive; the exclusive reading is the alternative.

research_rationale:
EO 12910 of April 23, 1994 (Providing for the Closing of Government Departments and Agencies on April 27, 1994), read in full in the held Federal Register text (59 FR 21915, Federal Register of April 26, 1994; machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (1994-04-23). Inventory: two operative provisions, each its own clause. Sec. 1 (characters 815 to 1271 of the held text) closes all executive departments, independent establishments and other governmental agencies, including their field services, on April 27, 1994 as a mark of respect for Richard Milhous Nixon, and treats that day as within the scope of 5 U.S.C. 6103(b) and of all statutes relating to the compensation and leave of employees. Sec. 2 (characters 1272 to 1653) provides that the first sentence of section 1 does not apply to offices and installations that the agency heads determine should remain open for reasons of national security or defense or other public reasons. The dossier's single clause covered Sec. 2 only; the inventory override adds Sec. 1 as its own clause. Legal reading: a one-day closing that ends by its own terms on April 27, 1994, recorded inclusive (the owner's until-date ruling of 2026-10-21 asks for the stated day inclusive and the exclusive reading stated; here the only day the order covers is April 27, 1994, so the exclusive reading is that the closing ends when that day begins). Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 1; the one catalog hit is the editorial disposition note "Note: In memoriam of President Nixon", which records no later event. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order: its one match is this order's own Federal Register text; the order's own text carries no wording signal beyond the stated day.
